sources.entry: Sleepless - Keeps your laptop awake with lid-closed support, auto-off timer, and battery-floor cutoff. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/Aboudjem/Sleepless)
Sleepless - Keep your MacBook awake with the lid closed, on battery, with no external display, with a battery-floor auto-off.

summary.what_it_does: It adds a single menu-bar switch that turns on a lid-closed, on-battery awake mode. An auto-off timer (1h or 2h, with a live countdown) turns the mode off automatically. A battery-floor cutoff, configurable from 5–50% on battery (default 15%), reverts the setting before the Mac drains flat. It also steps aside when Low Power Mode is on while on battery. The app reads the SleepDisabled flag back so the menu bar reflects the real state, and it reverts on reboot. Installation adds a sudoers rule that allows exactly two pmset commands without a password, so the GUI can flip the setting.
use_cases: Keep a MacBook running overnight with the lid closed
Finish builds, renders, or ML training while the laptop is closed
Leave large downloads, uploads, or backups running on battery
Share a phone hotspot from a closed laptop in a bag
Keep a local server or SSH session reachable with the lid shut
how_to_run: Alternatively: download the latest release, unzip to /Applications, and approve it under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway
Alternatively, build from source: git clone the repo, cd Sleepless, and run ./install.sh
Click the cup in the menu bar, flip the switch, and close the lid
notable: Uses pmset disablesleep, which the README says can keep the Mac awake with the lid closed where caffeinate-based apps cannot
Safety nets: battery-floor cutoff, Low Power Mode auto-off, timer, and reversion on reboot
Scoped sudoers rule limited to two exact pmset commands, with no daemon, helper script, or kext
Verifiable downloads via SHA256SUMS and gh attestation verify
No Dock icon and no background daemon
caveats: Ad-hoc signed and not notarized, so Gatekeeper requires manual approval unless built from source
Heavy sustained load with the lid closed can reduce airflow and overheat the Mac, so the README advises judgement
Behavior is described as hardware and macOS-version dependent
Not on the App Store; the README says the App Store verdict is covered in SECURITY.md
